title: Ethan Allen Draws Battle Lines, Rowe Takes the Sofa Outside
subtitle: A proxy fight sharpens over succession, a 91-year retailer closes its doors, and the handoff from screen to showroom floor gets a hard look.

content.title: Ethan Allen Draws Battle Lines, Rowe Takes the Sofa Outside
content.subtitle: A proxy fight sharpens over succession, a 91-year retailer closes its doors, and the handoff from screen to showroom floor gets a hard look.
content.greeting: Good morning. Ethan Allen filed its definitive proxy ahead of a November 4 shareholder vote, and the fight with DGB Investment is really a fight about who controls the next CEO search. Down in Holyoke, a 91-year-old furniture business is closing for reasons that will sound familiar to a lot of independents: rising prices, thin traffic, no cushion left. High Point previews keep arriving, from Rowe's outdoor cushion engineering to UE Living's anti-pinch motion tech. And a Furniture Today column on the conversion-versus-handoff debate cuts to something every store manager already knows: the sale is won or lost after the shopper walks in, not before.

top_stories.headline: Ethan Allen Files Its Proxy, Frames DGB as a Governance Risk
top_stories.summary: Ethan Allen (NYSE: ETD) filed its definitive proxy statement on September 24 ahead of a November 4 shareholder meeting, urging votes for CEO Farooq Kathwari's slate and against DGB Investment's nominees. The company conceded revenue sits below its 2006 peak but attributed roughly two-thirds of the fiscal 2026 decline to State Department, China and dealer revenue drops, not core retail weakness. It touted a five-year total shareholder return of 49.1% against a peer median of negative 42.7%, debt-free status and gross margin above 59%. For retailers watching the fight, the outcome will decide who runs the CEO search and whether Ethan Allen's manufacturing and logistics consolidation strategy continues or gets rewritten by an activist board.

top_stories.headline: Massachusetts Retailer Eddie's Furniture Closes After 91 Years
top_stories.summary: Eddie's Furniture Co. in Holyoke, Massachusetts is closing after 91 years, with owner Job Hicks citing rising prices, lack of federal funding and traffic that had nearly vanished since last summer. All inventory is being sold at 25% off, and Hicks will keep the doors open until it sells, after which he plans to sell the property, which realtors suggest could become an expanded parking lot. The business began as a horse barn in 1870 before Hicks' father started selling furniture in 1935. It is a stark reminder that independent retailers without pricing power or fresh traffic drivers are running out of runway, and that a strong local legacy no longer guarantees survival through a soft consumer stretch.

top_stories.headline: Rowe Expands Allteriors With Proprietary Outdoor Cushion
top_stories.summary: Rowe Furniture is expanding its Allteriors outdoor line, launched last April, with new textiles, tailored slipcovers and a proprietary down-alternative cushion built with quick-draining reticulated foam and antimicrobial fiber. President Bobby Robinson said the goal was extending Rowe's indoor silhouettes and comfort outdoors rather than building a separate outdoor category. The library now totals 47 outdoor performance fabrics, including 21 new textures sourced partly from Italy, and popular indoor pieces like Adler and Rothko are getting outdoor debuts. New introductions ship by the end of 2026 for Spring 2027. Retailers get a chance to sell outdoor as a design-forward extension of an already-trusted indoor brand rather than a discount seasonal category.

top_stories.headline: UE Living Debuts Anti-Pinch Motion Technology at High Point
top_stories.summary: UE Living is introducing SensoDrive, a motion upholstery technology with intelligent anti-pinch detection that pauses reclining motion when it senses an obstruction, at High Point Market. The feature will become standard across UE Living's modern, casual and transitional motion products at multiple price points, alongside whisper-quiet operation and double-tap reclining. General Manager Ron Yu said safety and comfort had to work together in the design. The showroom, in Furniture Plaza space 410, opens October 16. As motion upholstery becomes a larger share of upholstery sales, safety features that used to be premium extras are becoming baseline expectations, giving retailers a concrete talking point against private-label imports lacking the same engineering.

top_stories.headline: A Sales Rep's Take: Furniture's Problem Is the Handoff, Not Conversion
top_stories.summary: Furniture Today columnist Mike Root argues that the industry's conversion debate misses the real issue: by the time a shopper walks into a store, they have often already researched the product online, on social media or with AI, and the store visit is validation, not discovery. The failure point, he writes, is the handoff from marketing and technology to the sales floor, when an undertrained RSA cannot demonstrate a product a customer already knows about. Root, who trains associates on Cozzia massage chairs, says salespeople need enough confidence in a few key features, not mastery of every spec. The lesson for retailers: invest as seriously in floor training as in the marketing spend that drives traffic to the door.

industry_moves.headline: Ethan Allen Commits to Naming New CEO by June 2027
industry_moves.summary: Ethan Allen's board confirmed it is running a CEO succession process and will name a new chief executive no later than June 30, 2027, when Kathwari's current contract ends. Kathwari, CEO since 1988, will stay on as a non-executive board member through the 2027 annual meeting before stepping down entirely. An executive search firm is evaluating internal and external candidates. The timeline gives retailers and vendors a fixed date to watch as the DGB proxy fight plays out alongside the formal succession process.

industry_moves.headline: King Koil Gathers 17 Global Licensees in Shanghai
industry_moves.summary: King Koil held its first international licensee summit in Shanghai, bringing together more than 40 executives from 17 licensees across five continents under the banner "One King Koil, Stronger Together." CEO David Binke said the restructured business model has grown revenue, EBITDA and brand perception, with a goal of becoming a top-10 global bedding manufacturer. Executives previewed upcoming product innovations and shared U.S. retail engagement research. For licensees and retail partners, the consolidation signals a brand pushing further upmarket from its mass-market roots into premium and ultra-premium positioning.

industry_moves.headline: Retailers Tighten AI Oversight but Agentic Sprawl Keeps Growing
industry_moves.summary: A Netskope report finds ungoverned AI tool use among retail employees fell from 70% to 44% over the past year as more companies centralize tool approval, but 90% of employees still use AI trained on customer data. Retail-sector AI agents connecting to remote MCP servers jumped 400% during the survey period, and 56% of AI-related data violations Netskope tracked involved regulated customer data. For furniture retailers rolling out AI chat, design or inventory tools, the message is to pair adoption with visibility, since agentic tools are multiplying faster than most IT teams can track them.

retail_trends.headline: JCPenney's Furniture Sales Jump 41% Even as Total Revenue Falls
retail_trends.summary: JCPenney's overall net sales fell 8% to $1.3 billion in Q2, dragged down by apparel, but furniture led home category growth with a 41% increase versus last year. Gross margin rose to 39.2% from 38.7% despite higher product costs, and the retailer launched JCPenney Marketplace, adding third-party products to its website, with early results outperforming expectations. Net income fell 51% to $52 million. Furniture is proving to be a bright spot even inside a struggling department store, a signal that category demand exists for retailers willing to merchandise and price it well.

retail_trends.headline: Tapestry Lets Shoppers Buy Coach and Kate Spade Inside Gemini
retail_trends.summary: Tapestry now allows customers to purchase Coach and Kate Spade products directly inside Google's Gemini app and AI Mode using Google Pay, without leaving the chat, via the Universal Commerce Protocol. CEO Joanne Crevoiserat said the goal is reaching shoppers wherever inspiration strikes. Walmart and Ulta have made similar moves. With depending-on-the-source estimates putting online transactions at 30% to more than 40% of home furnishings sales, independents whose e-commerce share sits in the single digits should treat agentic checkout as the next front door, not a future problem, and start asking vendors whether their product data is even structured for AI discovery.

retail_trends.headline: Stitch Fix Warns Active Client Growth Won't Return in 2027
retail_trends.summary: Stitch Fix closed fiscal 2026 with net revenue up 6.4% to $1.3 billion but active clients down 1.4% year over year to just under 2.3 million, and executives told analysts they do not expect client growth to return in fiscal 2027. Net revenue per active client rose nearly 8% to $592, and the net loss narrowed 56% to $12.6 million. CEO Matt Baer said a tougher consumer environment is driving the caution. For subscription and personalization-driven home furnishings models, the lesson is that improving unit economics does not fix a shrinking customer base, and acquisition costs deserve as much scrutiny as retention.

supply_chain.headline: Amazon Adds AI Supply Chain Agents for Sellers
supply_chain.summary: Amazon is rolling out agentic AI capabilities inside Seller Assistant for inbound planning and aged inventory, with plans to expand into a full personalized supply chain advisor showing inventory location, proactive alerts and the data behind recommendations, VP Sunny Jain told Supply Chain Dive. Amazon is also building a unified shipment-tracking interface across fulfillment centers and consolidating compliance requirements by country, with pilot sellers reporting compliance cost savings up to 60%. For furniture sellers using Amazon or FBA-style fulfillment, this points toward inventory decisions increasingly made by AI rather than gut feel, raising the bar for suppliers who still ship on spreadsheets.

ai_tech.headline: Amazon Opens Seller Tools to Claude and Outside AI Agents
ai_tech.summary: Amazon is letting independent sellers run inventory, pricing and listing updates through Anthropic's Claude or its own Quick assistant instead of logging into Seller Central, with about 90% of sellers already using outside AI in some form. New background automations act on a seller's behalf with approval, and an upgraded Seller Assistant remembers pricing and inventory patterns over time. Furniture sellers on Amazon or similar marketplaces should expect listing and pricing management to shift toward AI agents quickly, and should audit whether their product data is clean enough for an agent to represent accurately.

ai_tech.headline: OpenAI Cuts Prices Sharply With GPT-6 Sol and Luna
ai_tech.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and Luna, priced roughly 50% cheaper per million tokens than prior versions, with Sol at $2 per million input tokens and Luna at 10 cents, while retaining much of flagship model Astra's coding and factuality gains. The move targets high-volume agentic workflows where token costs add up fast. For furniture retailers experimenting with AI for product descriptions, customer service or catalog tagging, cheaper capable models lower the cost of running those tools at scale across thousands of SKUs.

ai_tech.headline: Adobe Brings Photoshop and Firefly Tools Directly Into ChatGPT
ai_tech.summary: Adobe launched a plugin inside ChatGPT that unifies more than 70 tools from Photoshop, Firefly, Premiere, Express, Lightroom and Illustrator, letting users describe an edit or campaign asset and get finished creative without opening a separate app. Marketing and merchandising teams can generate consistent campaign imagery, product mockups and short-form video cuts from existing photography inside one conversation. For furniture brands and retailers producing room scenes, lifestyle shots and social content on tight budgets, this shortens the path from a single hero photo to a full campaign asset library.

one_thing.headline: Audit the Handoff From Ad to Associate
one_thing.body: Furniture Today's Mike Root makes the case that most lost sales happen after the shopper walks in already informed, not before. This week, sit in on three floor conversations and check whether the associate knows what the customer already researched online. If the handoff from marketing to the floor is weak, no amount of ad spend or AI shopping tool will fix the close.

content.closing: Monday's Brief will follow the Ethan Allen proxy fight toward its November 4 vote, track more High Point Market previews, and watch whether agentic checkout tools spread further into home furnishings retail.
